teaser.text: Exelon sells dependable access to electricity and natural gas through local delivery networks. Its customers pay for power to reach their premises, a meter to record use, and a utility responsible for maintenance and outage restoration.

stock.title: Exelon stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Exelon's weighted forecast is $42.91 by October 2029, with bear and bull outcomes shaped by regulation, cash flow and dilution.
stock.opening: Exelon's weighted scenario is $42.91 by October 2029, an 11% total return including dividends. It hinges on regulators approving investment, customers affording the resulting bills and large-load commitments becoming paying customers.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Exelon's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Exelon's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast sees limited near-term upside, followed by a more meaningful return if Exelon executes its investment plan. The probability-weighted price is $40.91 in October 2027, implying a 2% loss including dividends. It rises to $41.64 in October 2028, a 4% gain, and $42.91 in October 2029, an 11% gain.

The final-date outcomes are wide. The bear case reaches $29.09, while the bull case reaches $55.12. Today’s price is $43.50, so the central forecast remains cautious despite rising earnings and dividends.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Exelon?

paragraphs.text: The bear path starts at $2,730 million. It falls to $2,670 million before recovering to $2,700 million. This reflects delayed recovery, disallowed costs and financing pressure. The bull path starts at $3,150 million, then reaches $3,410 million and $3,650 million as rate-base expansion and project execution approach the upper end of management’s target. Net income rose each year from 2021 through 2025, supporting the base over the bear case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Exelon really make?

paragraphs.text: **Free cash flow** is operating cash flow minus capital spending. Exelon spent $8,529 million in 2025, leaving free cash flow of negative $2,275 million. Deducting $41 million of stock compensation produces real free cash flow of negative $2,316 million. That deduction recognizes the economic cost of issuing shareholders’ ownership to employees.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Exelon?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is what remains after capital spending. Exelon’s negative free-cash-flow yield signals a funding gap rather than distributable cash. The plan includes $3.4 billion of equity through 2029. That is about $850 million annually. Equity funds about 40% of incremental capital, and about 37% of those equity needs had been priced through forward contracts by July. At $43.50, $850 million would illustrate roughly 19.5 million shares. A forward contract prices a future sale; it does not mean those shares already exist. The useful test is therefore earnings per share, not total earnings.

dividend.title: Exelon dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: Exelon pays a $0.42 quarterly dividend, but negative free cash flow strains cash coverage; plans and risks could change it.
dividend.opening: Exelon pays a regular quarterly dividend, recently raised to $0.42 per share. Exelon’s cash does not currently cover that payout: 2025 free cash flow was negative $2,275 million against $1,617 million of dividends.
dividend.closing: The full Exelon memo also explains Exelon’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Exelon pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The balance sheet shows the cost of that choice. Net debt rose from $33,868 million at the end of 2021 to $49,454 million at the end of 2025. The board also increased the regular quarterly dividend to $0.42 per share on February 12, 2026. More income for shareholders means more cash to find alongside the investment programme, while higher interest expense reduces the benefit of improved operating results.

blocks.heading: Does Exelon’s dividend come from its cash?

paragraphs.text: Negative free cash flow does not automatically mean those investments failed. Free cash flow is the cash left after operations and capital spending, while regulators allow a utility to recover approved investment through customer bills over many years. But in 2025, negative free cash flow was $2,275 million and dividends were $1,617 million. Exelon therefore needed outside funding even before considering growth elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 2026 adjusted operating EPS of $2.81–$2.91. It targets 5%–7% annual adjusted EPS growth through 2029. The plan calls for $41,700 million of capital spending and 7.9% rate-base growth. Funding includes $3,400 million of planned equity through 2029, alongside a 5% annual dividend-growth target.
Exelon can grow EPS only if regulators approve investment, customers can afford the resulting bills and large-load commitments become paying customers.

earnings.title: Exelon earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Exelon’s next results are expected October 30, 2026; see its guidance, recent results and the regulatory recovery to watch.
earnings.opening: Exelon’s next results are expected on October 30, 2026. Watch whether regulatory recovery turns investment into customer-paid revenue.
earnings.closing: The full Exelon memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, Exelon guides to adjusted operating earnings of **$2.81–$2.91 per share**, based on **1,031 million average outstanding shares**. That share count matters because issuing stock makes per-share growth harder to achieve.

The longer target is **5%–7% annual compound growth from 2025 through 2029**, with performance expected near the upper end. Exelon measures that promise from the midpoint of its original 2025 guidance, **$2.69**, rather than its later reported adjusted earnings of **$2.77**. The fixed forecast starting point makes the promise easier to test, but it also means actual growth will look different if measured from what Exelon really earned.

paragraphs.text: Management did keep its financial promise. For 2025, adjusted earnings finished above the forecast range announced in February 2025. Exelon also reported top-quartile outage-duration performance at every utility. But fewer outages do not make electricity affordable, and the company must show that deferred work will not later damage reliability or increase costs.

blocks.heading: What have Exelon’s last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose to $5,967 million from $5,427 million for the comparable quarter. Operating income rose, but net income reached only $396 million and diluted EPS remained $0.39. Higher bills therefore did not translate proportionately into shareholders’ profit.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Exelon’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The most important milestones are regulatory decisions that turn completed investment into customer-paid revenue. BGE, Exelon’s Maryland utility, expects a decision on its pending electric rate case in **January 2027**. A rate case is the public review in which a utility requests recovery of costs and a return, while regulators and customer advocates test whether those amounts are justified.
